objective: Correct the CPVS parent metadata diagnostic so Type, Ng, and Nr are parsed according to the actual Table2 row representation rather than assumed byte offsets.
previous_knowledge_consumed: PR #176 already parses Table2 Seq/SourceID and maps published Table4 ZTF names to parent SourceIDs; exact membership remains unresolved.

PR #177 heavy artifact reports class_counts keys such as 0.00, which are not valid CPVS variable-type labels and indicate the diagnostic's fixed-byte Type extraction is incompatible with the acquired Table2 text mirror.
Official VizieR Table2 schema documents fixed-width byte offsets for the canonical CDS table, while the acquired Zenodo Table2.txt.zip may be a text mirror whose token positions differ.

baseline.status: Parent metadata diagnostics currently slice fixed-width offsets unconditionally; prior class-count output is not scientifically interpretable until the input layout is detected and parsed correctly.

expected_improvement: Parse the parent catalog's Type, Ng, and Nr using the same tokenization and ZTF-name/Seq interpretation that supports fixed-width and text-mirror rows.
Add regression coverage for whitespace-delimited Table2 text rows and split ZTF J-name representations.
Ensure class breakdowns contain actual source type labels and detection counts are read from the documented Ng/Nr columns.
Detect canonical fixed-width Table2 rows before using documented byte offsets; use token positions for text mirrors.

correctness.before: Fixed byte offsets produced numeric strings such as 0.00 as class labels on the acquired text mirror.
correctness.after: Metadata extraction uses validated token positions after handling the row's name representation; expected class labels and Ng/Nr values are tested.

regression_protection_count.before: No regression test checked parent metadata fields from the acquired text representation.
regression_protection_count.after: Two new tests assert Type, Ng, and Nr for tokenized and split-name rows.

evidence: The PR #177 heavy artifact's parent_catalog_context_diagnostic_only.class_counts contains keys like 0.00, which cannot be valid CPVS Type labels.
The previous metadata parser unconditionally read fixed byte offsets without confirming that the acquired parent rows used the canonical fixed-width layout.
The parser now validates fixed-width name/Seq/RA alignment before applying byte offsets, with a regression test containing a blank fixed-width field.
validation.blocker: Run focused tests, full CI, and a new source-backed heavy validation; verify real type keys and Ng/Nr counts before using these diagnostics to infer the remaining 11602 candidate-only objects.

findings: The diagnostic metadata parser assumed canonical CDS byte positions for every parent source representation. The acquired text mirror does not preserve those offsets, so class/Ng/Nr breakdowns were misparsed.
This defect affects diagnostic interpretation, not the existing CPVS candidate membership result or selection predicate.
Validate the physical representation before using byte offsets; fixed-width schema offsets cannot be applied blindly to whitespace-delimited text mirrors.
Do not interpret diagnostic summaries until parsed labels and field values pass schema-level assertions.
Keep diagnostics separate from selection policy and do not infer a root cause from mislabeled class/metadata counts.

open_blockers: Run the new parent metadata parsing regression tests and complete CI.
Run heavy source-backed validation and inspect refreshed class_counts and Ng/Nr summaries.
CPVS exact membership remains unresolved until the 11602 candidate-only IDs are explained.
Verify the fixed-width and text-mirror metadata tests both pass on the updated branch.

knowledge_carried_forward: Do not change the scientific selection predicate or frozen baseline to match a target count.
Only use candidate-only by-type/Ng/Nr analysis after confirming correct parsing of the acquired Table2 representation.
Keep PR #176/#177 unmerged until current-head CI and scientific evidence are reviewed.
